event_narrative: A brief, weak tornado touched down Thursday evening just south of|Wanchese on Roanoke Island. Video of the tornado was sent to the|office of a brief touchdown over the baseball fields of Pigum|Walker Park. The path consisted mainly of a mix of medium and|large limbs across the field. A bleacher was tossed about 10 to 15|feet into a concessions building where it then lifted toward the|parking lot. The concessions building lost shingles on both the|south and north side of the building, a strong indication of |rotation in this area, as confirmed by the video submitted to the |office. Peak wind speeds here were estimated at around 80 MPH.||A narrow and sporadic damage path continued to the southeast|across Brinkly Road, and near Old Schoolhouse Road. Damage here|again consisted of mainly medium sized limbs, but a few larger |limbs were noted. One tree was snapped halfway up the base but|were likely weaker due to disease in the middle, with winds |estimated around 75 MPH.||The path continued toward the southeast on Holly Lane, where a |medium, healthy tree was uprooted. Numerous medium to large |branches were found all along the path. While the tree was |uprooted to the south, numerous tree branches were bent back |toward the right of the path (or toward the east), confirming |rotation continued in this area. The damage path finally ended |near E R Daniels Road, where a shed was blown over, a few more |medium limbs were broken, and some horse training equipment was |blown over. Winds here likely weakened to 70 MPH.

episode_narrative: A coastal low formed off of the Southeast coast on October 11 and slowly tracked north into October 13 before moving offshore. Meanwhile, a strong area of high pressure lingered over the Gulf of Saint Lawrence. This resulted in a prolonged period of strong northeast winds and Storm conditions across the coastal waters on October 12.

episode_narrative: A rapidly deepening low pressure system off the Carolina Coast interacted with strong high pressure ridging centered in the Northeast which extended down into the Mid-Atlantic. As these two systems interacted, a tight pressure gradient resulted allowing for storm force wind gusts across the Eastern North Carolina Coastal Waters and the Pamlico Sound during the overnight hours of October eleventh through the morning hours of October Twelfth.

episode_narrative: A warm front lifted north across the waters of Eastern North Carolina during the afternoon hours of December 18th. Then as we got into the overnight hours between December 18th and 19th a coastal trough developed near the Outer Banks out ahead of an incoming cold front which was located to the west in central North Carolina at the time. Widespread showers and thunderstorms developing along this coastal trough. Some widely scattered thunderstorms become strong in nature bringing strong wind gusts to the coastal waters of the Core Banks, the offshore waters between Cape Lookout and Oregon Inlet, and portions of the Pamlico Sound.

event_narrative: Jennettes Pier XJNP WeatherFlow site measured several hours of frequent storm force wind gusts between the evening of January thirty-first and the morning of February first. Reports came in via the WeatherFlow site.
episode_narrative: A low pressure system developed along a baroclinic zone off the coast of Georgia during the overnight hours between Friday January 30th and Saturday January31st. This low then began to rapidly deepen during the evening hours of January 31st while tracking northeastwards along the Carolina Coast making its closest point of approach to the coastal waters near North Carolina during the early morning hours of Sunday February 1st with a minimum pressure around 994 mb before the system departed off to the north and east. With strong high pressure ridging building in from the north and west a tight pressure gradient spread over most of our waters bringing Storm Force wind gusts to much of the coastal and interior waters of eastern North Carolina during the evening of January 31st to the morning of February 1st.

episode_narrative: A low pressure area with a cold front attached to it tracked east across the Carolinas during the late morning and afternoon timeframe. Along and and out ahead of the cold front a line of scattered to numerous severe thunderstorms developed and quickly raced east northeast across Eastern NC, producing 60 to 70 mph wind gusts. With ample instability and strong wind shear in place several of the storms interacted with the sea breeze inland from the coast and produced several tornadoes, in addition to severe thunderstorm wind damage.

episode_narrative: A strong cold front began tracking east from lee of the Appalachians to the Triad region of North Carolina during the late morning and afternoon hours of Monday March Sixteenth. Out ahead of this front, a prefrontal trough developed across the Coastal Plain. With ample moisture, instability, as well as low level and deep layer wind shear noted across North Carolina, scattered shower and thunderstorm activity developed along and out ahead of the prefrontal trough. Given the favorable conditions a few of the thunderstorms became strong in nature producing a mix of waterspouts and strong wind gusts across  the Pamlico, Croatan, Roanoke, and Albemarle sounds and coastal waters north of Ocracoke Inlet.

episode_narrative: An unusually strong low pressure system swung through southern Virginia, dragging a cold front across Eastern North Carolina and offshore by the evening hours. Ahead of it, bands of thunderstorms formed in the afternoon due to unstable conditions and wind shear in place. Scattered severe wind gusts embedded in some of the storms impacted portions of the Albemarle and Pamlico Sound as well as the coastal waters north of Oregon Inlet.

episode_narrative: A coastal trough combined with the daily seabreeze and a second inland trough to produce multiple rounds of shower and thunderstorm activity through the day and into the evening hours on June twenty-seventh. With ample instability and deep layer shear in place some of these thunderstorms became strong to severe in nature bringing a strong and damaging wind threat to the waters mainly north of the Crystal Coast.
